findings.summary: crates/athena-data/src/records/throughput.rs is not a measure-only module, so the path trigger refuses readings that change no measure, and a corpus case would pin that false positive.
findings.evidence: Read crates/athena-data/src/records/throughput.rs: module doc line 1 is 'Throughput-review, build-measurement and Hestia-sweep records.'; it defines ThroughputReview (100), SccacheCounts (181), BuildMeasurement (218), HestiaSweep (328), DutyPass (357), all record types with no computation. check_durations, which the plan places there, is actually at crates/athena-core/src/status/throughput.rs:63. HISTORY.txt lines 86-100: 3a25c33 'Make Hestia's sweep own and schedule Athena's recurring duties' touched it because DutyPass and HestiaSweep live there. It is evidence of a false positive, not of a missed measure change. The same commits also count toward the 8-of-200 estimate behind the declared 3%. Fix: Remove crates/athena-data/src/records/throughput.rs from RECORDS_MEASURE_PATHS and keep crates/athena-core/src/status/throughput.rs and status/planning.rs, whose module docs say they compute figures. Rebuild the path-trigger corpus case on a status/throughput.rs or status/planning.rs deliverable, not on 3a25c33. Correct Decision 1's evidence and the share estimate, and add an accepted case showing that a reading with records/throughput.rs as a deliverable and no measure word is not refused by check_records_measure.
findings.location: Decision 1 / Approach (b) PATHS; plan step 7 corpus case measure-module-path-no-measure-word

findings.summary: Bare 'time spent' is common English and will refuse unrelated code readings, such as 'reduce time spent waiting for CI'.
findings.evidence: The plan narrows bare 'throughput' to records phrases for exactly this reason but leaves 'time spent' bare. HISTORY.txt shows it once as a measure name (line 1233). The measure it names is time_spent in status/throughput.rs:452, which the path trigger already covers. Fix: Narrow 'time spent' as 'throughput' was narrowed (for example 'unlanded time spent', 'time spent per job', or the identifier time_spent), or drop it and rely on the status/throughput.rs path trigger. Add a corpus or unit case that accepts a CI-wait 'time spent' reading.

findings.summary: Pure move or split refactors that create a measure module are path-triggered, the cost the plan rejected status.rs for.
findings.evidence: HISTORY.txt line 309/313: cf59590 'Split status.rs into modules and shorten status() under limits' created crates/athena-core/src/status/throughput.rs. Athena queues such code-health split jobs itself. Fix: Either state in the doc comment and CHANGELOG that code-health splits of these modules need the criterion too (a moved figure can change), or exempt readings whose summary declares a move with no behavior change. Pin whichever choice with a corpus case.

findings.summary: This job's own accepted reading would be refused by the new check, which the dependents and the replay estimate do not mention.
findings.evidence: Criterion 3 is a [behavior] criterion containing 'landing time' and has no real-records criterion. It does not contain 'newly refused', so the skip does not apply, and the reading is code class with a capability. Fix: Note in the Dependents entry for the replay that this job's own reading is among the newly refused, and count it in the share estimate, so the verifier's replay figure is not a surprise.
findings.location: Criterion 3 of this job's own reading; Dependents 'readings newly refused when stored readings are replayed'

findings.summary: The no-growth assertion is stricter than the size test needs; the 'reader 2 tokens left' premise refers to the budget set, which excludes READING_RULES.
findings.evidence: briefs.rs:3555-3558 records 3045 bytes with a limit of < 3150. crates/athena-context/src/lib.rs has no READING_RULES reference in BudgetSet, consistent with the 'Prompt sets and budgets' system fact. Fix: Keep the conservative choice if wanted, but say in the test comment that the bound is the < 3150 section limit, not the reader budget set, so later readers do not misattribute it.

summary: The plan is mostly sound and grounded in the code. Checked by reading: refusing_check and its step! lines (checks.rs:518-546); the measure functions keep_rule (planning.rs:242), planning_cost (planning.rs:304), time_spent (throughput.rs:452) and landed_jobs (throughput.rs:472); git log in ENV_LOCATED_SOURCES with history.json absent from it; the evidence snapshot giving producer and verifier records/, landings/ and history.json (briefs.rs:657-667); and the drain and steward routing of failing stored readings, already pinned by tests (drain.rs:4406, steward.rs:2755). Out-of-deliverable files are justified and Athena already flagged them. One major soundness fault: crates/athena-data/src/records/throughput.rs is one of the three 'measure-only' path triggers, but it holds record types (throughput reviews, build measurements, Hestia sweeps, duty passes) and no measure code. The commit offered as evidence of a missed measure change, 3a25c33 (Hestia duty scheduling), is in fact a false positive, and the planned corpus case built from it would pin that false positive as intended. Smaller points: bare 'time spent' matches common English; module-split refactors are path-triggered; and this job's own reading would be refused by the new check in the replay.
